name: Venus Flytrap
intro: A Venus flytrap is a small plant that catches bugs. Its leaves snap shut like a trap.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A Venus flytrap is a small green plant.
Its leaves grow in a circle.
Each leaf ends in a trap with two halves.
Tiny trigger hairs grow inside the trap.
Spiky bristles line the edges of the trap.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Venus flytraps grow wild in North Carolina and South Carolina.
They live in wet, sunny places like bogs.
The soil there is wet most of the year.
That soil has very little plant food.
Fires help keep their homes open and sunny.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A Venus flytrap needs lots of sun.
It needs wet soil.
It makes food from sunlight like other plants.
It also catches bugs to get extra nutrients.
It mostly eats ants and spiders.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A Venus flytrap grows from a tiny black seed.
In late spring, it grows white flowers.
The flowers sit on a tall stalk, away from the traps.
Each trap can close only a few times.
Then the plant grows a new trap.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A trap snaps shut very, very fast.
A hair must be touched two times to close the trap.
This way, raindrops do not trick the trap.
A trap cannot hurt people.
A Venus flytrap can live up to 20 years.

vocab.meaning: A plant that catches and eats bugs.
